extracted.intended_audience: DoD financial managers, acquisition officers, policy analysts, and military WCF activity managers
extracted.subtask_description: Assessing appropriateness and application of OMB Circular A-76 competitive sourcing studies to revenue-generating functions in Defense Working Capital Fund (DWCF) activities, including process steps, standards, metrics, and DWCF-specific considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary objectives of the A-76 process
rubrics_metrics.description: Three fundamental principles define the goals of the A-76 process: Achieve economy and enhance productivity; Keep inherently governmental functions 'in-house'; Rely on commercial sector for products and services if determined economical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose is to move non-inherently-governmental commercial activities to private sector when economical, freeing government to focus on core inherently governmental activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1996 A-76 revision policy elements
rubrics_metrics.description: The 1996 revision added: Balance the interests of the parties to make or buy cost comparisons; Provide a level playing field between public and private offerors to a competition; Encourage competition and choice in the management and performance of commercial activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revision focused on initiating competition for new/expanded work based on an A-76 cost comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1999 A-76 revision provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Circular A-76 (1999) outlines: the government may engage in commercial activities if critical to combat or mission effectiveness; a commercial source is not available or cannot meet requirements in time; another federal agency can provide the goods/services; procuring from commercial firms will result in higher cost than internal production; inherently governmental items are excluded from outsourcing consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are conditions under which agencies may retain or procure functions; intended to clarify limits and exceptions to outsourcing under A-76.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assumption of competitive markets
rubrics_metrics.description: A-76 assumes there will be competitive markets with many competing suppliers capable of providing and bidding for business. If competitive markets do not exist, OMB should reevaluate use of A-76.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If competition is absent, applying A-76 can create non-value added costs; packaging and market analysis should detect this risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: A-76 twelve-step process (overall)
rubrics_metrics.description: A comprehensive 12-step process: 1) Packaging & Commercial Activity Identification; 2) Public Announcement; 3) Formulation of PWS & QASP; 4) Solicitation; 5) Creation of Government Management Plan; 6) Independent Review; 7) Negotiation Phase; 8) Selection of a Single Provider; 9) Cost Comparison; 10) Administrative Appeals; 11) Implementation of MEO or Contractor Organization; 12) Post A-76 Actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process typically takes 18–36 months depending on complexity; each step has specific required documents, reviews, and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 1 — Packaging / business unit definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Packaging (business unit definition) decides which commercial activities comprise the cost comparison and structures them into business units suitable for competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective packaging maximizes future competition. Bundle similar functions to create competitive bids; separate independent functions. Consider asset specialty, complexity and frequency. Incorrect packaging limits contractor ability to compete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 2 — Public announcement
rubrics_metrics.description: A public announcement notifies Congress, local community, and local federal workforce that a commercial activity is under competition under A-76 and starts the timeline. The Unit Commander appoints a study team leader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification responsibilities and appointing oversight are required; complex operations may require outside consultants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 3 — Performance Work Statement (PWS)
rubrics_metrics.description: The PWS outlines product requirements, timeframes, performance measures and standards; it describes the work performed and the results required, forming the basis of the RFP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Developing an accurate PWS is critical; a poor PWS can render the study unproductive by failing to express true organizational requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 3 — Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan (QASP)
rubrics_metrics.description: QASP describes procedures to verify the selected proposal meets PWS requirements, focusing on product quality rather than procedures, and uses metrics and performance measures for cost comparisons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: QASP defines inspection methods, required reports, resources, and performance metrics; it applies regardless of whether MEO or contractor wins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 4 — Solicitation / RFP requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Solicitation includes pre-acquisition steps: choose contract type, create source selection plan, develop evaluation criteria, develop independent cost estimate, prepare and release RFP. The RFP must specify final award be solely on cost comparisons with in-house providers and must include a 'First Refusal of Employment' clause for in-house employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no private bids are received, the government retains the function but must still implement the MEO. RFP must make clear the cost-comparison basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 5 — Government Management Plan and its documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Government Management Plan describes the Government's Most Efficient Organization (MEO) and forms the basis for the In-House Cost Estimate (IHCE). It includes MEO, IHCE, Technical Performance Plan (TPP), and Transition Plan (TP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These documents must identify organizational structures, staffing, operating procedures, equipment, transition and inspection plans to show government can perform in the most efficient manner.

rubrics_metrics.name: MEO (Most Efficient Organization) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The MEO contains the government estimate for performing the commercial activity in-house, outlining proposed organizational structure, administrative and staffing functions, and operating procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MEO lays foundation for IHCE; MEO must be realistic and implementable — errors here propagate.

rubrics_metrics.name: IHCE (In-House Cost Estimate) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The IHCE contains the cost estimate for the MEO and describes all costs associated with performance (overhead, staffing, severance, miscellaneous). It also lists organic assets not provided to the contractor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IHCE is developed solely on the MEO; if the MEO is incorrect the IHCE is incorrect. All costs must be justified and documented.

rubrics_metrics.name: TPP (Technical Performance Plan) and TP (Transition Plan)
rubrics_metrics.description: TPP details how the government will carry out PWS requirements if the activity remains governmental. TP outlines transition process to MEO or contractor including personnel, equipment transfer, inventories, and procedural changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TP is implemented after final selection; transition planning is required whether MEO or contractor selected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 6 — Independent Review (IRO) responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: An Independent Review Officer evaluates the PWS, QASP, MEO, IHCE, TPP, and TP to ensure requirements are adequate and realistic and that costs determined by the IHCE are justified. IRO should be an official not involved in development of the Government Management Plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IRO ensures government capability to perform described function with identified resources; IRO provides independent checks on fairness and realism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 7 — Negotiation phase and selection process (contract discussions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting Officer conducts written/oral discussions with private bidders per FAR to resolve discrepancies in cost proposals; CO selects a single firm based on ability to meet MEO requirements. Selection in this phase uses 'best value' rather than later 'cost comparison' method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Negotiations must follow FAR; best value selection considers overall value to government in response to solicitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 8 — Cost comparison criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Source Selection Authority compares the in-house MEO/IHCE with the selected private sector proposal; ensures both proposals provide same scope and level of performance. The final selection is based on lowest cost after ensuring performance parity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If government in-house proposal is deficient it must be revised for a fair comparison. The aim is equivalent performance so selection is cost-driven.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum cost differential requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a minimum cost differential requirement: the contractor proposal must be 10% lower than the Government proposal or $10M less over the performance period, whichever is less, to win. If not, the function remains in government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differential accounts for conversion costs to a private contractor when savings are small; threshold must be passed before tentative decision to outsource.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 9 — Administrative appeals rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals must be in writing and received by the contracting officer within the review period. Only contractors who submitted proposals, federal employees eligible for replacement, or government agencies eligible for replacement may submit appeals. Appeals most frequently concern cost comparison issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeal process focuses on alleged errors in the cost-comparison and related steps; timely, documented appeals are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 10/11 — Implementation and Post-MEO Performance Review
rubrics_metrics.description: After appeals, the selected entity (MEO or contractor) begins the Transition Plan; if MEO is implemented, a formal review and inspection occurs after the first full year to confirm implementation per the Transition Plan and that actual costs align with IHCE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-MEO Performance Review verifies MEO's ability to perform PWS services and cost conformity; QASP is implemented and periodically reviewed to ensure PWS validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 12 — Post A-76 actions and ongoing QASP
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon completion of A-76 the new organization begins full performance and QASP is implemented regardless of final choice. QASP is periodically reviewed; formal review of MEO occurs at end of first year if MEO implemented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ongoing performance oversight and periodic QASP reviews are required to maintain service quality and compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitation contingency — no private bids
rubrics_metrics.description: If an A-76 solicitation results in no bids from the private market, the Government automatically retains the function but still must implement the MEO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even without contractor offers, the A-76 process requires implementing documented improvements via MEO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement of A-76 savings (effectiveness metrics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Historical A-76 savings have often been measured by reduction in Civil Service Full Time Equivalent (FTE) personnel and percentage savings (reduction of FTE dollar amounts over total budget). Example reported averages: ~30% savings (FTE-based) in studies through 1996; Navy Strategic Sourcing reported average savings 43.6% for completed cost comparisons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data presented primarily reflect personnel savings; operational savings beyond FTE reduction may be undocumented. Beware of attributing routine management savings to A-76 over multi-year study periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to ensure 'level playing field' between public and private offers
rubrics_metrics.description: A-76 policy requires providing a level playing field between public and private offerors during competition so comparisons are fair.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes standardized evaluation metrics, consistent scope (PWS), and objective cost accounting in IHCE and contractor proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: DWCF full cost recovery principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Under a revolving fund full cost recovery concept, stabilized prices and rates are set at the beginning of the fiscal year for each business area to break even; business areas will experience positive or negative Net Operating Results (NOR); consolidation yields Accumulated Operating Result (AOR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DWCF components strive for break-even AORs. This accounting model affects how DWCF activities price services and evaluate efficiencies versus A-76 assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: DWCF — Annual Operating Budget (AOB)
rubrics_metrics.description: AOB is a funding document providing the basis for earning budgetary authority; it identifies every unit cost output and its associated unit cost goal; released by Under Secretary of Defense (Comptroller).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AOB sets unit cost goals that DWCF activities must meet; impacts pricing and internal assessments of efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: DWCF — Unit Cost (UC) definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Unit Cost (Cost per Output) is the relationship of resources consumed to outputs produced: Unit Cost = Cost of Resources / Number of Outputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UC is baseline for establishing prices and assessing DWCF performance; accurate workload and cost allocation are essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: DWCF — Unit Cost Goal (UCG)
rubrics_metrics.description: UCG is the maximum allowable cost to be incurred in producing an output; derived by dividing projected costs (direct, indirect, G&A) by expected workload; issued by Under Secretary of Defense (Comptroller).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UCG functions as a pricing/performance constraint and competitiveness benchmark for DWCF activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: DWCF — Cost of Goods Sold (COG)
rubrics_metrics.description: COG represents the average acquisition cost of items sold, obtained for each NSN by spreading acquisition investment over inventory; matches sales revenue with transactions affecting costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: COG is the baseline for operating results and establishing prices; not affected by surcharge rates or net outlays.

rubrics_metrics.name: DWCF — Net Operating Result (NOR) and Accumulated Operating Result (AOR)
rubrics_metrics.description: NOR is the positive/negative operating result for a business area during budget execution; AOR consolidates all business area NORs. Components strive for break-even AOR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitoring NOR/AOR is fundamental to DWCF financial health and pricing decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: DWCF — Operating Budget and Capital Budget definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Operating Budget contains annual operating costs (including depreciation/amortization, major maintenance). Capital Budget authorizes acquisition of capital assets (depreciable property, equipment, software) over $100,000 with useful life ≥2 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budgetary classifications determine how costs appear in IHCE and influence pricing and investment decisions relevant to A-76 comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: DWCF — Capital Assets definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Capital assets are depreciable property, plant, equipment, and software developed/acquired at cost ≥ $100,000, used over a period (useful life ≥2 years), and generally become economically worthless except residual value at useful life end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classification of assets affects IHCE, charge-outs, and contractor proposals when assets are or are not provided to contractor.

rubrics_metrics.name: DWCF — Pricing on cost vs market consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: DWCF is currently pricing products based on cost of operations, not on what the market will bear; recommendation for further research on defining costs, cost allocation systems, and pricing strategies to compete better while covering cost of operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When DWCF prices by cost rather than market, A-76 comparisons that assume market pricing may misjudge competitiveness; pricing strategy affects perception of pre-competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to verify pre-competition / market competition in DWCF
rubrics_metrics.description: Research recommendation: verify what portions of DWCF are truly pre-competed and which have market competition before applying A-76.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understanding actual market exposure of DWCF functions is necessary to determine appropriateness of A-76.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inherently Governmental Function #1 — Direct conduct of criminal investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: The direct conduct of criminal investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inherently Governmental Function #2 — Control of prosecutions and adjudicatory functions
rubrics_metrics.description: The control of prosecutions and performance of adjudicatory functions (other than those relating to arbitration or other methods of alternative dispute resolution).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inherently Governmental Function #3 — Command of military forces
rubrics_metrics.description: The command of military forces, especially the leadership of military personnel who are members of the combat, combat support or combat service support role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inherently Governmental Function #4 — Conduct of foreign relations and foreign policy determination
rubrics_metrics.description: The conduct of foreign relations and the determination of foreign policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inherently Governmental Function #5 — Determination of agency policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The determination of agency policy, such as determining the content and application of regulations, among other things.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inherently Governmental Function #6 — Determination of Federal program priorities or budget requests
rubrics_metrics.description: The determination of Federal program priorities or budget requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inherently Governmental Function #7 — Direction and control of Federal employees
rubrics_metrics.description: The direction and control of Federal employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inherently Governmental Function #8 — Direction and control of intelligence and counter-intelligence operations
rubrics_metrics.description: The direction and control of intelligence and counter-intelligence operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inherently Governmental Function #9 — Selection/non-selection for federal employment
rubrics_metrics.description: The selection or non-selection of individuals for Federal Government employment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inherently Governmental Function #10 — Approval of position descriptions and performance standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The approval of position descriptions and performance standards for Federal employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inherently Governmental Function #11 — Determination of Government property disposition
rubrics_metrics.description: The determination of what Government property is to be disposed of and on what terms (although agencies may give contractors authority to dispose of property at prices within specified ranges and subject to other reasonable conditions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inherently Governmental Function #12a — Procurement: determining supplies or services to be acquired
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Determining what supplies or services are to be acquired by the Government (although an agency may give contractors authority to acquire supplies at prices within specified ranges and subject to other reasonable conditions deemed appropriate by the agency).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inherently Governmental Function #12b — Procurement: participation as voting member on source selection boards
rubrics_metrics.description: (b) Participating as a voting member on any source selection boards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inherently Governmental Function #12c — Procurement: approval of contractual documents
rubrics_metrics.description: (c) Approval of any contractual documents, to include documents defining requirements, incentive plans, and evaluation criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inherently Governmental Function #12d — Procurement: awarding contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: (d) Awarding contracts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inherently Governmental Function #12e — Procurement: administering contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: (e) Administering contracts (including ordering changes in contract performance or contract quantities, taking action based on evaluations of contractor performance, and accepting or rejecting contractor products or services).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inherently Governmental Function #12f — Procurement: terminating contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: (f) Terminating contracts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inherently Governmental Function #12g — Procurement: determining reasonableness/allocability/allowability of contract costs
rubrics_metrics.description: (g) Determining whether contract costs are reasonable, allocable, and allowable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inherently Governmental Function #13 — Approval of FOIA responses (non-routine)
rubrics_metrics.description: The approval of agency responses to Freedom of Information Act requests (other than routine responses that do not require exercise of judgment) and approval of responses to administrative appeals of FOIA denials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inherently Governmental Function #14 — Conduct of administrative hearings affecting security clearances or reputation
rubrics_metrics.description: The conduct of administrative hearings to determine eligibility for a security clearance, or involving actions that affect personal reputation or eligibility to participate in Government programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inherently Governmental Function #15 — Approval of federal licensing actions and inspections
rubrics_metrics.description: The approval of Federal licensing actions and inspections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inherently Governmental Function #16 — Determination of budget policy, guidance, strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: The determination of budget policy, guidance, and strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inherently Governmental Function #17 — Collection, control, and disbursement of public funds (with limited exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The collection, control, and disbursement of fees, royalties, duties, fines, taxes and other public funds, unless authorized by statute (with exceptions such as routine collection at mess halls, exchanges, parks and routine voucher/invoice examination).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Routine collections and certain voucher/invoice examinations are excluded from being inherently governmental.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inherently Governmental Function #18 — Control of the treasury accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: The control of the treasury accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inherently Governmental Function #19 — Administration of public trusts
rubrics_metrics.description: The administration of public trusts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance on asset specialty and supplier lock-in risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Packaging and outsourcing decisions must recognize implications of asset specialty and the danger of supplier dominance (asset specificity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High asset specificity risks locking the government into supplier dominance and should be considered in packaging and make-or-buy decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation to account for time-lagged savings attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: From baseline inventory until end of A-76 study 3–4 years could pass; research should evaluate how much savings occurred through routine management decisions during that time that are credited to A-76 but did not derive from it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When measuring A-76 effectiveness, adjust for savings realized by routine management over multi-year durations to avoid over-attribution to A-76.
